zh: “你们去是去，”古应春半真半假地警告：“当心《申报》登你们的新闻。”“喔，”胡雪岩突然提高了声音说：“应春提到《申报》，我倒想起一件事来了。从去年冬天天津到上海的电报通了以后，我看《申报》上有些新闻是打电报回来的。盛杏荪当电报局总办，消息格外灵通，有些生意上头，我们消息比人家晚，哪怕只不过晚一步，亏就吃得很大了。所以，我有个念头，应春，你看能不能托《申报》的访员帮忙？”“是报行情过来？”“是啊。”“那，我们自己派人在天津，每天用密码发过来好了。”“那没有多少用处。”胡雪岩说：“有的行情，只有访员才打听得到。而且，也不光是市面上的行情，还有朝廷里的行情。象去年冬天，李大先生的参案……“
en: “You may go,” Gu warned, half in jest, “but take care that your adventures do not appear in the Shen Bao.” “Ah!” Hu suddenly raised his voice. “That mention of the Shen Bao reminds me of something. Since the Tianjin–Shanghai telegraph opened last winter, I have noticed that some of its news arrives by wire. With Sheng Xingsun directing the telegraph administration, he is exceptionally well informed. In certain kinds of business, if our news comes later than his—even one step later—we can suffer a serious loss. I have been wondering, Yingchun, whether we could obtain help from the newspaper's reporters.” “To telegraph market quotations?” “Yes.” “Then why not station someone of our own in Tianjin and have him send a daily report in cipher?” “That would be of limited use. There are things only reporters can discover. Besides, I do not mean merely conditions in the market. I mean conditions at court too. Take the impeachment of the elder Mr Li last winter…”

zh: “李大先生，”是指李瀚章。七姑奶奶的性情，外粗内细，一听谈到这些当朝大老的宦海风波，深知有许多有关系的话，不宜为不相干的人听见，传出去会惹是非，对胡雪岩及古应春都没有好处，所以悄悄拉了罗四姐，同时还做了个示意离席的眼色。“他们这一谈就谈不完了，我们到旁边来谈我们的。”罗四姐极其知趣，立刻迎合着七姑奶奶的意向说：“我也正有些话，不便当着他们谈。七姐，我心里头有点发慌。”“为啥？”罗四姐不即回答，将七姑奶奶拉到一边，在红丝绒的长安乐椅上并排坐了下来，一只手执着七姑奶奶的手，一只手只是摸着因酒而现红晕的脸。“是不是身子不舒服？”七姑奶奶不安地问：“怎么好端端地，心里会发慌？”“不是身子不舒服。”罗四姐仿佛很吃力他说：“我做梦也没有想到，忽然会有象今天这样子一天，又遇见雪岩，又结识了七姐你，好比买‘把儿柴’的人家，说道有一天中了‘白鸽票’，不晓得怎么好了。”七姑奶奶虽是松江人，但由于胡雪岩的关系，也憧杭州话，罗四姐的意思是，升斗小民突然中了奖券，也就是拿穷儿暴富的譬喻，来形容她自己的心境。七姑奶奶觉得她的话很中听，原来就觉得她很好，这下便更对劲了。不过要找一句适当的话来回答倒很难，所以她只是笑嘻嘻地说：“怎么会呢？怎么会呢？”
en: The elder Mr Li was Li Hanzhang. For all her outward bluntness, the Seventh Lady was inwardly perceptive. Once the conversation turned to the political fortunes of senior statesmen, she knew that many consequential remarks ought not to be overheard by people unconnected with the matter. If repeated, they might cause trouble for both Hu and Gu. She quietly drew Luo Sijie aside, signalling with her eyes that they should leave the table. “Once they begin, they will talk for ever. Let us go over there and have our own conversation.” Luo immediately understood and cooperated. “I have things to say that I would rather not discuss before them. Seventh Sister, I feel rather unsettled.” “Why?” Instead of answering, Luo led her to a long red-velvet easy chair, where they sat side by side. With one hand she held the Seventh Lady's; with the other she kept touching her wine-flushed cheeks. “Are you unwell?” the Seventh Lady asked anxiously. “Why should you suddenly feel unsettled?” “It is not that.” Luo seemed to find the words difficult. “I never dreamed that a day like this would come: meeting Xueyan again, and getting to know you. I feel like a family that buys its firewood a handful at a time and suddenly wins a prize in the White Pigeon lottery. I hardly know what to do.” Though a native of Songjiang, the Seventh Lady understood Hangzhou expressions through her acquaintance with Hu. Luo meant that an ordinary poor person had suddenly won a fortune. The comparison pleased her. She had liked Luo already and now felt still closer to her. Finding a suitable reply was difficult, however, so she merely smiled and said, “Surely not! Surely not!”

zh: “怎么不会？我一个寡妇，哪里有过这种又说又笑又吃酒的日子。他要帮我开绣庄，你要请我逛堂子，不要说今生今生，前世都不曾想到过的。”踌躇满志之意，溢于言表，七姑奶奶当然看得出来，抓住她一只手，合拢在那那双只见肉、不见骨的温暖手掌中，悄悄问道：“罗四姐，他要帮你开绣庄，不过一句话的事，你的意思到底怎么样呢？”罗四姐不答，低垂着眼，仿佛有难言之隐，无法开口似地。“你说一句嘛！愿意就愿意，不愿意就不愿意，勉强不来的事。”“我怎么会。不愿意呢？不过，七姐，”罗四姐倏然抬眼，“我算啥呢？”“女老板。”“出本钱是老板，本钱又不是我的。”七姑奶奶始而诧异，做现成的老板，一大美事，还有什么好多想的？继而憬然有悟，脱口说道：“那么是老板娘？”罗四姐又把头低了下去。幽幽地说：“我就怕人家是这样子想法。”不说自己说人家，言外之意就很微妙了。遇到这种时候，七姑奶奶就不会口没遮拦了，有分寸的话，她拿把握住分寸，才肯出口。
en: “Why not? When has a widow like me ever had a day of talking, laughing, and drinking like this? He offers to help me open an embroidery shop, and you offer to take me to a courtesan house. I could never have imagined such things in this life—or even a previous one.” Her delight was unmistakable. Taking one of Luo's hands between her own warm, plump palms, the Seventh Lady quietly asked, “Helping you open a shop would take no more than a word from him. What do you really think of it, Sister Luo?” Luo lowered her eyes without replying, as though troubled by something she could not express. “Say something. If you want it, you want it; if you do not, you do not. Nobody can force you.” “How could I not want it? But, Seventh Sister…” She suddenly looked up. “What would that make me?” “The proprietor.” “The person who supplies the capital is the proprietor. The capital would not be mine.” At first the Seventh Lady was puzzled. Becoming the owner of a ready-made business was a wonderful opportunity; why hesitate? Then understanding dawned. “The proprietor's wife, then?” Luo lowered her head again. “That is exactly what I fear people would think.” By speaking of other people rather than herself, she conveyed a subtle implication. At such moments the Seventh Lady was far from indiscreet. She would not venture a delicate remark until she had judged its precise effect.

zh: “罗四姐，”她终于开口探问了，“你年纪还轻，又没有儿女，守下去没有意思嘛。”在吃消夜以前，罗四姐原曾谈过身世。当时含含糊糊表示过，没有儿女，此时听七姑奶奶这样说，她觉得应该及时更正。才显得诚实。“有个女儿。”她说，“在外婆家。”“外婆在哪里？”“杭州。”“女儿不比儿子，总是人家的。将来靠女婿，他们小夫妇感情好还好，不然，这碗现成饭也很难吃。尤其是上有婆婆，亲家太太的脸嘴，实在难看。”“我是决不会靠女婿的。”罗四姐答说，声音很平淡，但字字清楚，显得很有把握。“那么你靠哪个呢？”“靠自己。”
en: “You are still young, Sister Luo,” she finally said, testing the ground. “And with no children, what is the point of remaining a widow?” Before supper, Luo had spoken of her past, vaguely implying that she had no children. Hearing this repeated, she felt she should correct it at once to demonstrate her honesty. “I have a daughter,” she said. “She lives with her maternal grandmother.” “Where is her grandmother?” “Hangzhou.” “A daughter is different from a son. In the end, she belongs to another family. Depending on a son-in-law may be tolerable if the young couple get along well, but otherwise that ready-provided meal can be hard to swallow. Especially if his mother is still living: the looks a daughter's mother receives from her fellow mother-in-law can be very unpleasant.” “I shall never depend on a son-in-law,” Luo replied. Her voice was calm, each word clear and confident. “Whom will you depend on, then?” “Myself.”

zh: “靠自己就更要有一样靠得住的东西了。”意在言外，是劝她接受胡雪岩的资助，但罗四姐就在这一顿消夜前后，浮动在心头的各种杂念，渐渐凝结成一个宗旨：要接受胡雪岩的好处，就不止于一家绣庄，否则宁可不受。因而明知其意，却装作不解。七姑奶奶当然不相信她不懂这话，沉默不答，必是别有盘算，便追问着说：“你说我的话是不是？靠自己是有志气的事，不过总也要有一样东西抓在手里。绣花这样本事，全靠年纪轻、眼睛亮、手底下准，没有几年，你就靠不住了。”靠得住的便是绣庄。罗四姐不会再装不懂了，想一想说：“要说开绣庄，我再辛苦两三年，邀一两个姐妹淘合伙，也开得起来。”莫非是嫌胡雪岩的忙帮得不够？还是性情耿介，不愿受人的好处？七姑奶奶一时还看不出来，便也就保持沉默了。“七姐，”罗四姐忽然问道：“胡家老太太还在？”“健旺得很呢。”七姑奶奶问：“你见过？”“见过。”“那么，胡太太呢？也见过？”“也见过。”罗四姐忽然幽幽地叹了口气。这一下，七姑奶奶恍然大悟。胡雪岩未忘旧情，罗四姐旧情未忘。胡雪岩那边不会有什么障碍，如果罗四姐这方面肯委屈，倒也未始不是一件美事。感情上的事，要两厢情愿。七姑奶奶当时便作了个决定，给他们机会，让他们自己去接近。果然有缘，两情相洽，那时看情形，再来做现成媒人，也还不迟。
en: “Then you need something dependable all the more.” The Seventh Lady meant that Luo should accept Hu's financial assistance. But during supper, the various thoughts drifting through Luo's mind had gradually crystallized into a resolution: if she accepted anything from Hu, it must be more than an embroidery shop. Otherwise, she would accept nothing. Understanding perfectly, she pretended not to. The Seventh Lady did not believe she had missed the meaning; silence must conceal some further calculation. “Am I not right? It is admirable to rely on yourself, but you must have something secure in your hands. Embroidery depends on youth, clear eyesight, and accurate fingers. In a few years, you will no longer be able to rely on them.” The dependable alternative was plainly a shop. Luo could not continue pretending incomprehension. After a pause, she said, “As for opening an embroidery shop, if I work hard for another two or three years and bring in one or two women friends as partners, I can manage it myself.” Did she consider Hu's offer insufficient, or was she too proud and upright to accept favours? The Seventh Lady could not yet tell and fell silent. Luo suddenly asked whether Hu's mother was still alive. “Very much alive and vigorous. Have you met her?” “Yes.” “And Mrs Hu? Have you met her too?” “Yes.” Luo gave a soft sigh. Now the Seventh Lady understood completely. Neither Hu nor Luo had forgotten their former affection. There would be no obstacle on his side; if Luo were willing to accept a less exalted position, the arrangement might prove a happy one. Affection required willingness on both sides. She decided to give them opportunities to draw closer on their own. If their feelings truly accorded, there would still be time to act as matchmaker once matters had developed.

zh: “阿七，”古应春在喊，“小爷叔要走了。”七姑奶奶转脸看时，小大姐已在伺候胡雪岩穿马褂了，“小爷叔，”她说：“今天不算数，明天晚上我正正式式请罗四姐，你有没有空？”胡雪岩尚未答话，罗四姐抢在前面谦谢，“七姐，七姐，”她说，“你太客气了。”“不是客气，道理上应该。”七姑奶奶奶又说：“就算客气，也是这一回。”罗四姐不作声了，胡雪岩便笑着问她说道：“你看，七姐就有这点本事，随随便便一句话就能够把你的嘴封住，没话可说。”“我话还是有的，”罗四姐说：“恭敬不如从命。”“你这话。”七姑奶奶说道：“才真的太客气了。”“那么，还有句不客气的话：只此一回，下不为例。”“好，好。下不为例。”古应春与胡雪岩互相看了一眼，有同感的默契，罗四姐也是个角色，针锋相对，口才上并不逊于七姑奶奶。
en: “A'qi!” Gu called. “Little Uncle is leaving.” Turning, the Seventh Lady saw the maid helping Hu into his riding jacket. “Little Uncle, today does not count. Tomorrow evening I shall formally entertain Sister Luo. Are you free?” Before he could answer, Luo protested politely. “Seventh Sister, you are much too kind.” “It is not excessive kindness. It is only proper. And even if it is a formality, it will be the only time.” Luo fell silent. Hu smiled at her. “That is one of Seventh Sister's talents. A casual sentence, and she closes your mouth, leaving you nothing to say.” “I still have something to say: obedience is better than excessive courtesy.” “Now that,” the Seventh Lady replied, “really is too polite.” “Then here is something less polite: just this once, and no precedent.” “Very well. No precedent.” Hu and Gu exchanged a glance of shared understanding. Luo was a woman of mettle too, matching the Seventh Lady's wit point for point.

zh: “闲话少说，”七姑奶奶问道：“小爷叔，明天晚上你到底有没有空？”“没有空，也要抽出空来啊！”“罗四姐，你看，你多少有面子！”“哪里，我是沾七姐你的光。”“地方呢？”胡雪岩插嘴问说。“你看呢？”七姑奶奶征询丈夫的意见，“我看还是在家里吧！”“也好。”“那就说定了。”七姑奶奶又说：“小爷叔，还有句话，我要言明在先。罗四姐今天住在我这里，明天早晨，我送她回去，下午再去接她，不过。晚上送她回家，小爷叔，是你的差使了。“这是试探罗四姐，如果她对胡雪岸没有意思，一定会推辞，一个男人，深夜送单身女子回家，那会在邻居之中引起极多的批评，罗四姐果真以此为言，七姑奶奶是无法坚持一定要胡雪岩送的。推辞也很容易，最简捷的办法，便是说夜深不便，仍旧想住在古家。可是，她不是这样说，说的是：“胡大先生应酬多，不要再耽误他的工夫了。”“没有，没有！”胡雪岩赶紧接口：“明天晚上我没有应酬。”七姑奶奶看着罗四姐笑了，这一笑倒使得她有些发窘，将视线避了开去。
en: “Enough talk,” the Seventh Lady said. “Are you free tomorrow evening or not, Little Uncle?” “Even if I am not, I shall make time.” “See what consideration he shows you, Sister Luo!” “I merely benefit from your influence.” “Where shall we dine?” Hu asked. The Seventh Lady consulted her husband. “At home, I think?” He agreed. “Then it is settled. But I must make one thing clear beforehand. Sister Luo is staying here tonight. Tomorrow morning I shall take her home and fetch her again in the afternoon. Taking her home tomorrow night, Little Uncle, will be your responsibility.” This tested Luo's feelings. If she had no interest in Hu, she would certainly object. A man escorting an unattached woman home late at night would provoke much comment among the neighbours. If she raised that objection, the Seventh Lady could not insist. Refusal would also be easy: she could simply say that it would be inconvenient to return so late and that she wished to stay at the Gu house again. Instead, she said, “Mr Hu has so many engagements. We ought not to take up more of his time.” “None! None!” Hu answered quickly. “I have no engagement tomorrow evening.” The Seventh Lady smiled at Luo, who grew a little embarrassed and looked away.

zh: 第二天，七姑奶奶送罗四姐回家，她家住南市，一楼一底的古库房子，这条弄堂是小康之家集居之地。楼上住家，楼下客厅。客厅中已坐满了人，大多挟着一个平平扁扁的包裹，有个中年妇女首先迎上来埋怨似地说：“罗四姐，你昨天一天哪里去了？我儿子要看病，急着要交货等钱用。““喔。”罗四奶歉然答说：“昨夜我住在我姐姐那里。”谁也没有听说过罗四姐有个姐姐，所以不免好奇地注视七姑奶奶，看她一副富态福相，衣服华丽不说，腕上一双翠镯，指上黄豆大一枚闪光耀眼的金刚钻戒指，便使得大家另眼相看了。七姑奶奶却毫无架子，而且极其爽郎，“你先不要招呼我，大家都在等你。”她对罗四姐说：“你赶紧料理，我来帮你。”“再好没有。”罗四姐高叫：“老马，老马！”老马是她请的帮手，五十多岁，帮她管帐兼应门，有时也打打杂，人很老实，但语言木讷，行动迟缓。这么多交货领货的人，无以应付，索性在厢房里躲了起来，此时听得招呼，方始现身。平时收货发货，只有罗四姐跟他两个人，这天添了一个帮手，便顺利得多，但也一直到中午，方能毕事。“真对不起。”罗四姐说，“累你忙了半天。”接着便关照老马，到馆子里叫菜，要留七姑奶奶吃饭。
en: The next morning the Seventh Lady took Luo home. She lived in Nanshi, in a two-storey stone-gated house on a lane inhabited by comfortably situated families. The living quarters were upstairs and the reception room below. The latter was already crowded, most of the visitors carrying flat parcels. A middle-aged woman approached first, sounding reproachful. “Where were you all yesterday, Sister Luo? My son needs a doctor. I am waiting to deliver my work and get the money.” “Oh!” Luo replied apologetically. “I stayed at my sister's last night.” Nobody had heard that she had a sister, and everyone looked curiously at the Seventh Lady. Her prosperous appearance and fine clothes were impressive enough; the pair of jade bracelets at her wrists and the dazzling diamond ring, its stone as large as a soybean, inspired still greater respect. Yet she was entirely unassuming and cheerful. “Do not attend to me. Everyone is waiting. Get on with your work, and I shall help.” “Nothing could be better! Old Ma! Old Ma!” Old Ma was her assistant, a man in his fifties who kept the accounts, answered the door, and occasionally did odd jobs. Honest but slow in speech and movement, he had been unable to cope with so many people delivering and collecting work and had simply hidden in a side room. Only when called did he emerge. Normally Luo and he handled all the receiving and issuing themselves. With another pair of hands, things went more smoothly, but it was still noon before they finished. “I am so sorry to have kept you working all morning,” Luo said. She told Old Ma to order food from a restaurant, intending to keep her guest for lunch.

zh: “你不必客气，我来认一认地方，等下再来接你。家里还有事要料理，我索性楼上都不上去了，下半天来了再来看你的卧房。”这在罗四姐倒是求之不得，因为卧房中难免有凌乱不宜待客之处。“既然这么说，我也不留七姐了。”她说：“下半天七姐派车子来好了，自己就不必劳驾了。明天晚上，我请七姐、七姐夫来吃便饭，不晓得七姐夫有没有空。”“等下再说好了。”客人一走，罗四姐便从容了，吃过饭，她有午睡的习惯。一觉醒来，想起胡雪岩晚上要来，当即唤小大姐，连老马都叫了上来，帮着拖地板、抹桌子、擦窗户，换了干净的被褥，又把一套平时难得一用的细瓷茶具亦找了出来，另外备了四个果盘。等预备停当，开始妆扮，好在她一向是一张清水脸，只加意梳好一个头，便可换衣服坐等了。等到五点钟，只听楼下人声，小大姐匆匆忙忙奔上来说：“胡老爷来了。”罗四姐没有想到是他来接，好在都已经预备好了，不妨请他上楼来坐。于是走到楼梯口说道：“胡大先生，怎么劳你的驾？要不要上来坐一坐。““好啊！”影随声现，罗四姐急忙闪到一边。江浙两省，男女之间的忌讳很多，在楼梯上，上楼时必是男先女后，下楼正好相反，因为裙幅不能高过男人头顶，否则便有“晦气”。罗四姐也是为此而急忙闪汗，等胡雪岩上了楼梯，她已经亲自打着门帘在等了。
en: “There is no need. I came to learn where you live and shall return to fetch you later. There are things to arrange at home. I shall not even go upstairs now; I can see your room this afternoon.” Luo welcomed this, for her bedroom was bound to contain some untidiness unsuitable for a visitor. “Then I shall not detain you. Just send a carriage this afternoon; you need not trouble to come yourself. Tomorrow evening I should like you and Brother-in-Law Gu to have a simple meal here. I wonder whether he is free.” “We can discuss that later.” Once her guest had gone, Luo could relax. After lunch she took her customary nap. On waking, she remembered that Hu would come that evening and summoned the maid and Old Ma to help scrub the floor, wipe the tables, and clean the windows. She changed the bedding, brought out a fine porcelain tea service seldom used, and prepared four dishes of fruit and nuts. Then she dressed. Since she normally wore no makeup, she needed only to arrange her hair with particular care before changing her clothes and sitting down to wait. At five, voices sounded below, and the maid hurried upstairs. “Mr Hu has come.” Luo had not expected him to fetch her himself. Fortunately everything was ready, so she could invite him upstairs. At the stairhead she called, “How kind of you to come, Mr Hu. Would you like to sit upstairs for a moment?” “Gladly!” His figure followed his voice, and she quickly stepped aside. Jiangsu and Zhejiang observed many restrictions between men and women. On stairs, a man must ascend first and a woman follow; descending, the order was reversed. A woman's skirt must not rise above a man's head, or it would bring him bad luck. That was why she moved aside. By the time he reached the top, she was holding the door curtain for him herself.

zh: 胡雪岩进了门，先四周打量一番，点点头说：“收拾得真干净，阳光也足，是个旺地。”“寡妇人家，又没有儿子，哪里兴旺得起来？”胡雪岩没想到她一开口就是很直也很深的话，一时倒不知该持何态度？便只好笑笑不答。这时小大姐已倒了茶来，罗四姐便照杭州待客之礼，将高脚果盘中的桂圆、荔枝、瓜子、松子糖之类，各样抓一些，放在胡雪岩面前，一个说：“不好吃。”一个连声：“谢谢。”“罗四姐，有点小意思。你千万要给我一个面子。”胡雪岩又说：“跟我来的人，手里有个拜匣，请你关照小大姐拿上来。”取来一个乌木嵌银丝的拜匣，上面一把小小的银丝，钥匙就系在搭扣上，打开来看，里面是三扣“经折”，一个小象牙匣子。
en: Entering, Hu looked around and nodded. “How neatly everything is kept. Plenty of sunlight too. An auspicious place.” “A widow's household, without even a son—how prosperous can it become?” He had not expected so direct and suggestive an opening and could not decide how to respond. He merely smiled. The maid brought tea. Following Hangzhou hospitality, Luo took a little of everything from the stemmed dishes—dried longans, lychees, melon seeds, and pine-nut sweets—and placed it before him. She modestly declared the refreshments unworthy, while he repeatedly thanked her. “I have a small token for you, Sister Luo. You must do me the honour of accepting it. The man who came with me is carrying a presentation box. Please ask the maid to bring it up.” The box was ebony inlaid with silver wire, with a small silver lock and its key tied to the clasp. Inside lay three folded account books and a little ivory case.

zh: 胡雪岩先拿起两扣，一面递给罗四姐，一面交代：“一个是源利的，一个是汪泰和的。”源利与汪泰和是上海有名的两家大商号，一家经营洋广杂货，一家是南北货行。罗四姐接过经折来看，户名是“阜康钱庄”，翻开第一页，上面用木戳子印着八个字：“凭折取货，三节结帐，”意思是罗四姐不管吃的、穿的、用的，凭折到这两家商号随便索取，三节由阜康付帐。这已经是厚惠了，再看另一扣经折，罗四姐不由得心头一震，是一扣阜康的定期存折，存银一万两，户名叫做“维记”。“本来想用‘罗记’，老早有了，拆开来变‘四维记’哪晓得这个户名也有了，只好把‘四’字搁起，单用‘维记’。喏，（编注：”罗“字繁体为‘ ’。）胡雪岩拿起小象牙匣子，”外送一个图章。“罗四姐接过经折与牙章，放在桌上，既非辞谢，亦未表示接受，只说：“胡大先生，你真的阔了。上万银子，还说小意思。”“我不说小意思，你怎么肯收呢？”“我如果不收，你一定要跟我争，空费精神。”罗四姐说：“好在送不送在你，用不用在我。这三个经折，一颗图章，就放在我这里好了。”她做事说话，一向胸有丘壑，胡雪岩认为不必再劝，便即说道：“那么，你把东西收好了，我们一起走。”
en: Hu picked up two of the books and handed them over. “One is for Yuanli; the other for Wang Taihe.” These were two of Shanghai's celebrated large firms, one dealing in imported and Cantonese general merchandise, the other in produce from north and south. Luo opened the books. Both accounts were in Fukang Bank's name, and the first page bore a stamped instruction: goods could be obtained against the book, with settlement at the three annual festivals. Whatever she needed to eat, wear, or use, she could collect from either firm; Fukang would pay. This was generous enough. But the third book made her heart leap: it recorded a fixed-term deposit of ten thousand taels at Fukang under the name Weiji. “I had intended to call it Luoji, but that name was already taken. Splitting the written surname Luo into its components suggested Siweiji, but that account name existed too. So I dropped Si and kept Weiji. Here…” (An editorial note in the supplied text refers to the traditional form of Luo, but the character it is meant to display is missing.) He picked up the little ivory case. “A seal to go with it.” Luo took the book and ivory seal and set them on the table. Neither declining nor explicitly accepting, she merely said, “You really have become wealthy, Mr Hu. Ten thousand taels, and you call it a small token.” “If I did not, how could I persuade you to take it?” “If I refuse, you will argue, and we shall waste our energy. Fortunately, whether to give is your decision, and whether to use it is mine. I shall keep the three books and the seal here.” Her words and actions always followed a considered design. Hu felt no further persuasion was needed. “Then put them away safely, and let us go.”

zh: “怎么走法？”“你下去就晓得了。”胡雪岩是坐轿子来的，替罗四姐也备了一乘很华丽的轿子，他想得很周到，另外还加了一顶小轿，是供她的女仆或小大姐乘坐的。胡雪岩还带了三个跟班，簇新的蓝布夹袍，上套玄色软缎坎肩，脚下薄底快靴。由于要骑马的缘故，夹袍下摆都掖在腰带中，一个个精神轩昂，礼节周到。罗四姐也很好面子，心里不由得在想：出门能带着这样子的“底下子”，主人家自然很显得威风了。正要上轿时，罗四姐忽然想到一件事，还得回进去一次。原来她是想到应该备礼送古家，礼物现成，就是绣货。送七姑奶奶的是两床被面、一对枕头、一堂椅被、两条裙子，这已经很贵重了，但还不如送古应春的一条直幅，是照宋徽宗画的孔雀，照样绣下来的，是真正的“顾绣”。到得古家，展现礼物，七姑奶奶非常高兴，“你这份礼很重，不过我也不客气了。”她说：“第一，我们的日了还长，总有礼尚往来的时候。第二，我是真正喜欢。”当时便先将绣花椅披，陈设起来，粉红软缎，上绣牡丹，显得十分富丽。
en: “How are we going?” “You will see when you go downstairs.” Hu had arrived by sedan chair and provided a particularly handsome one for Luo. Thoughtfully, he had also brought a smaller chair for her woman servant or young maid. Three attendants accompanied him in new blue lined robes, black satin waistcoats, and light, thin-soled boots. Since they rode horses, the skirts of their robes were tucked into their belts. Each looked alert and carried himself with impeccable courtesy. Luo cared about appearances too. She could not help thinking how imposing an employer would look with such attendants when going out. Just as she was about to enter the chair, she remembered something and returned inside. She ought to bring gifts to the Gu household, and embroidery was ready to hand. For the Seventh Lady she selected two coverlets, a pair of pillows, a set of chair covers, and material for two skirts. Valuable as these were, they were surpassed by the gift for Gu: a vertical embroidered panel copied from Emperor Huizong's painting of a peacock, a genuine example of Gu embroidery. When the gifts were displayed at the Gu house, the Seventh Lady was delighted. “These are substantial presents, but I shall not stand on ceremony. First, we have many years ahead of us, and opportunities to return one another's kindness. Second, I truly like them.” She immediately had the chair covers arranged. Peonies embroidered on pink satin gave the room a rich splendour.

zh: “七姐，”罗四姐说：“你比一比这两条裙子的料子看，是我自己绣的。”一条是红裙，上绣百蝶，色采繁艳，令人眩目，“好倒是好，不过我穿了，就变成‘丑人多作怪’了。”七姑奶奶说，“这条裙子，要二十左右的新娘子，回门的时候穿，那才真叫出色。我留起来，将来给我女儿。”“啊！”胡雪岩从椅子上一下站了起来，大声说道：“应春，你要请我吃红蛋了？”原来古应春夫妇，只有一个儿子，七姑奶奶却一直在说，要想生个女儿。胡雪岩看她腰身很粗，此刻再听她说这话，猜想是有喜了。古应春笑笑不答，自然是默认了。罗四姐便握七姑奶奶的手说：“七姐，恭喜，恭喜！几个月了。”七姑奶奶轻声答了句：“四个月。”“四个月了！唷、唷，你赶快给我坐下来，动了胎气，不得了。”“不要紧的。洋大夫说，平时是要常常走动走动，生起来才顺利。”“ 唷！七姐，你倒真开通，有喜的事，也要请教洋大夫。”罗四姐因为七姑奶奶爽朗过人，而且也没有外人，便开玩笑地问：“莫非你的肚皮都让洋大夫摸过了。”“是啊！不摸怎么晓得胎位正不正？”原是说笑，不道真有其事，使得罗四姐挢舌不下，而七姑奶奶却显得毫不在乎。“这没有啥好稀奇的，也没有啥好难为情的。”“叫我，死都办不到。”罗四姐不断摇头。“罗四姐！”古应春笑道：“你不要上她的当，她是故意逗你。洋大夫倒是洋大夫，不过是个女的。”“我说呢！”罗四姐舒了口气，“洋人那只长满黑毛，好比熊掌样的手，模到你肚皮上，你会不怕？”
en: “Seventh Sister, hold these skirt lengths against yourself. I embroidered them.” One was red, covered with a hundred butterflies in dazzling colours. “It is beautiful, but on me it would be an ugly woman making a spectacle of herself,” the Seventh Lady said. “A bride of about twenty, returning to visit her parents, would look splendid in it. I shall keep it for my daughter.” Hu sprang from his chair. “Yingchun! Will you be inviting me to eat red eggs?” The couple had only one son, but the Seventh Lady had often spoken of wanting a daughter. Hu had noticed her thickened waist, and her words now made him suspect that she was expecting. Gu smiled without answering, tacitly confirming it. Luo took the Seventh Lady's hand. “Congratulations! How many months?” “Four,” she answered softly. “Four months! Quickly, sit down. It would be dreadful to disturb the baby.” “It is all right. The foreign doctor says I should walk about regularly to make the birth easier.” “How broad-minded you are, consulting a foreign doctor even about pregnancy!” With no outsiders present, and knowing her companion's frankness, Luo teasingly asked whether she had even allowed the doctor to feel her belly. “Of course. How else could the doctor tell whether the baby was lying properly?” Luo had meant it as a joke; discovering it was true left her speechless. The Seventh Lady was quite unconcerned. “There is nothing strange or shameful about it.” Luo shook her head repeatedly. “I could never do that, even if I died.” Gu laughed. “Do not let her deceive you, Sister Luo. She is teasing. The doctor is indeed foreign—but a woman.” “I thought as much!” Luo breathed with relief. “Would you not be afraid of a foreign man's hand, covered in black hair like a bear's paw, touching your belly?”

zh: 七姑奶奶付之一笑，拿起另一条裙子料子看，月白软缎，下绣一圈波浪，上面还有两只不知名的鸟。花样很新，但也很大方。“这条裙子我喜欢的，明天就来做。”七姑奶奶兴致勃勃地说：“穿在身上，裙幅一动，真象潮水一样。罗四姐，你是怎么想起来的。”“也是我的一个主顾，张家的二少奶奶，一肚子的墨水，她跟我很投缘，去了总有半天好谈。有一天不知道怎么提起来一句古话，叫做‘裙拖六幅湘江水’，我心里一动，回来就配了这么一个花样。月白缎子不耐脏，七姐，我再给你绣一条，替换了穿。”“这倒不必，我穿裙子的回数也不多。”这时古应春跟胡雪岩在看那幅“顾绣”，开屏的孔雀，左右看去，色彩变幻，配上茶花、竹石，令人观玩不尽，胡雪岩便说：“何不配个框子，把它挂起来？”“说得是。”古应春立刻叫直听差来吩咐：“配个红木框子，另外到洋行里配一面玻璃。最好今天就能配好。”“接着又看被面、看枕头，七姑奶奶自己笑自己，说是”倒象看嫁妆“。惹得婢仆们都笑了。
en: The Seventh Lady merely smiled and took up the other skirt length. It was pale blue satin, embroidered along the lower edge with waves and, above them, two birds she could not identify. The design was both novel and graceful. “I like this one. I shall have it made tomorrow. When the skirt moves, it will look just like a flowing tide. How did you think of it?” “One of my customers, the Zhang family's second young mistress, is very learned. We get along so well that whenever I visit, we talk for half a day. Once, somehow, she mentioned an old line: ‘Her six-panelled skirt trails the waters of the Xiang.’ It gave me an idea, and I designed this when I went home. Pale blue satin soils easily. I shall embroider another for you to alternate with it.” “There is no need. I do not wear skirts very often.” Meanwhile, Hu and Gu were examining the Gu embroidery. Viewed from different angles, the spread-tailed peacock's colours changed. Camellias, bamboo, and rocks completed a composition that rewarded endless attention. “Why not frame it and hang it?” Hu suggested. Gu immediately summoned a servant and ordered a rosewood frame, with a sheet of glass obtained from a foreign trading house, preferably that very day. They next examined the coverlets and pillows. Laughing at herself, the Seventh Lady said it was almost like inspecting a trousseau, which made the servants laugh too.

zh: “饿了！”胡雪岩问：“七姐，快开饭了吧？”“都预备好了，马上就开。”席面仍旧象前一天一样。菜是古应春特为找了个广东厨子来做的，既好又别致，罗四姐不但大快朵颐，而且大开眼界，有道菜是两条鱼，一条红烧、一条清蒸，摆在一个双鱼形的瓷盘中，盘子也很特别，一边白，一边黄，这就不仅罗四姐，连胡雪岩都是见所未见。“这叫‘金银鱼’，”古应春说，“进贡的。”胡雪岩大为诧异，“哪个进贡？”他问，“鱼做好了，送到宫里，不坏也不好吃了。”“自然是到宫里，现做现吃。”古应春说，“问到是什么人进贡，小爷叔只怕猜不到，是山东曲阜衍圣公进贡的。”“啊！”胡雪岩想起来了，“我听说衍圣公府上，请第一等的贵客，菜叫‘府菜’，莫非就是这种菜？”“一点不错。府菜一共有一百三十六样，菜好不奇稀，奇的是每样菜都用特制的盘碗来盛。餐具也分好几种，有金、有银、有锡、有瓷，少一样，整桌台面都没用了，所以衍圣公府上请贵客，专有个老成可靠的老家人管餐具。”“那么进贡呢？当然是用金台面？”“这是一定的。”古应春又说：“宫里有喜庆大典，象同治皇帝大婚，慈禧太后四十岁整生日，衍圣公都要进京去道喜、厨子、餐具、珍贵的材料都带了去。须先请旨，预备哪一天享用府菜，到时候做好送进宫，有的菜是到宫里现做，这要先跟总管太监去商量，当然也要送门包。好在衍圣公府上产业多，不在乎。”
en: “I am hungry,” Hu said. “Can we dine soon?” “Everything is ready. We shall begin at once.” The arrangement was much as on the previous evening, but Gu had specially engaged a Cantonese cook. The dishes were excellent and unusual, delighting Luo's palate and broadening her experience. One consisted of two fish, one red-braised and one steamed, on a double-fish-shaped porcelain platter, one side white and the other yellow. Even Hu had never seen anything like it. “Gold and Silver Fish,” Gu explained. “A dish presented as tribute.” “By whom?” Hu asked in surprise. “By the time cooked fish reached the palace, even if it had not spoiled, it would no longer taste good.” “Naturally, it is cooked there and eaten fresh. As for who presents it, you might never guess: the Duke Yansheng of Qufu in Shandong.” “Ah!” Hu remembered. “I have heard that his household serves its most distinguished guests what is called ‘household cuisine.’ Is this an example?” “Exactly. There are a hundred and thirty-six dishes. Their quality is no surprise; what is remarkable is that each requires a specially made plate or bowl. The service includes gold, silver, pewter, and porcelain. If one piece is missing, the whole table setting is unusable. When the duke entertains distinguished guests, a dependable old family servant has sole charge of the tableware.” “And for imperial tribute, surely the service is gold?” “Certainly. At great palace celebrations, such as the Tongzhi emperor's wedding or Cixi's fortieth birthday, the duke goes to Beijing to offer congratulations, taking his cooks, tableware, and rare ingredients. Permission must first be sought for a day on which the court will enjoy his household cuisine. The food is prepared and delivered at the appointed time, though some dishes are cooked inside the palace itself. That requires advance arrangements with the chief eunuch—and naturally a gratuity for gaining access. Fortunately, the duke's estates are extensive, so he need not worry about the expense.”

zh: 胡雪岩听了大为向往，“应春，”他问：“你今天这个厨子，是衍圣公府出身？”“不是，他是广东人，不过，他的爷爷倒是衍圣公府出身。这里面有段曲折，谈起来蛮有趣的。”说着，他徐徐举杯，没有下文。“喔，”七姑奶奶性急，“有趣就快说，不要卖关子！”“我也是前两天才听说，有点记不太清楚了，等我好好想一想。”“慢慢想。”罗四姐挟了块鱼敬他，“讲故事要有头才好听。”“好！先说开头，乾隆未年……”乾隆来年，毕秋帆当山东巡抚。阮元少年得意，翰林当了没有几年，遇到“翰詹大考”，题目是乾隆亲自出的，“试帖诗”的诗题是“眼镜”。这个题目很难，因为眼镜是明朝未年方由西洋传入中土，所以古人诗文中，没有这个典故，而且限韵“他”字，是个险韵，难上加难，应考的无不愁眉苦脸。考试结果，阮元原为一等第二名，乾隆拔置为第一，说他的赋做得好，其实是诗做得好，内中有一联：“四目何此，重瞳不用他”，为乾隆激赏，原来乾隆得天独厚，过了八十岁还是耳聪目明，不戴眼镜，平时常向臣下自诩。因此，阮元用舜的典故“四目”、“重瞳”来恭维他，意思是说他看人看事，非常清楚，根本用不着借助于眼镜。
en: Hu was much attracted by this account. “Did today's cook come from the duke's household?” “No, he is Cantonese. But his grandfather did. There is an interesting story behind it.” Gu slowly raised his glass and said no more. “If it is interesting, tell us!” his impatient wife urged. “Do not keep us waiting.” “I only heard it a couple of days ago and cannot quite remember. Let me think.” “Take your time.” Luo offered him a piece of fish. “A story is best when it has a proper beginning.” “Very well. To begin: late in Qianlong's reign…” Bi Qiufan was then governor of Shandong. Ruan Yuan had enjoyed early success and been in the Hanlin Academy only a few years when a major examination of Hanlin and Household of the Heir Apparent officials was held. Qianlong himself set the questions. The prescribed subject for the examination poem was spectacles. It was difficult: spectacles had entered China from the West only late in the Ming, so ancient poetry and prose offered no established allusion to them. Moreover, the required rhyme was ta, an awkward choice that made the task harder still. Every candidate looked distressed. Ruan was originally placed second in the first class, but Qianlong promoted him to first, saying that his rhapsody was excellent. In fact, it was the poem that pleased him, particularly a couplet to the effect that four eyes had no need of these things, and double pupils had no use for them. The emperor had been unusually favoured by Heaven: even after eighty, his hearing and eyesight remained keen, and he wore no spectacles, a fact of which he often boasted to his ministers. Ruan had used the allusions to Shun's four eyes and double pupils to flatter him, implying that he perceived people and affairs so clearly that spectacles were unnecessary.

zh: 大考第一，向来是“连升三级”，阮元一下子由编修升为詹事府少詹，不久就放了山东学政，年纪不到三十，继弦未娶。毕秋帆便向阮元迎养在山东的“阮老太爷”说：“小女可配衍圣公，请老伯做媒，衍圣公的胞姐可配令郎，我做媒。”阮元就此成了孔家的女婚。衍圣公府上的饮撰，是非常讲究的，因为孔子“食不厌精”，原有传统。因此，随孔小姐陪嫁过来的，有四名厨子，其中有一个姓何，他的孙子，就是古应春这天邀来的何厨。“那么，怎么会是广东人呢？”胡雪岩问。“阮元后来当两广总督，有名的肥缺，经常宴客，菜虽不如府菜，但已经远非市面上所及。不过不能用‘府菜’的名目，有人便叫它‘满汉全席’。总督衙门的厨子，常常为人借了去做菜，这何厨的爷爷，因此落籍，成为广东人。“
en: First place in this examination traditionally brought promotion through three grades. Ruan rose at once from Hanlin Compiler to junior supervisor in the Household of the Heir Apparent, and soon became educational commissioner of Shandong. Still under thirty, he had lost his wife and had not remarried. His father had come to live with him there. Bi Qiufan told the elder Ruan, “My daughter could marry the Duke Yansheng; I should like you to arrange it. The duke's elder sister could marry your son; I shall arrange that match.” Thus Ruan became a son-in-law of the Kong family. The duke's household paid particular attention to food, following the tradition of Confucius, who did not consider food too finely prepared. Four cooks therefore accompanied Miss Kong as part of her marriage establishment. One was surnamed He; his grandson was the cook Gu had engaged that day. “How, then, did he become Cantonese?” Hu asked. “Ruan later became Governor-General of Liangguang, a famously lucrative post, and entertained frequently. Although the food did not equal the duke's household cuisine, it far surpassed anything available commercially. Since the household name could not be used, some called it the Manchu–Han Grand Banquet. The Governor-General's cooks were often borrowed to prepare meals elsewhere. That is how Cook He's grandfather settled in Guangdong, and the family became Cantonese.”

zh: 正谈到这里，鱼翅上桌，只见何厨头戴红缨帽，列席前来请安。这是上头菜的规矩，主客照例要犒赏，胡雪岩出手豪阔，随手拈了张银票，便是一百两银子。“这盘鱼翅，四个人怎么吃得下？”罗四姐说，“我真有点替七姐心痛。”鱼翅是用二尺五口径的大银盘盛上来的，十二个人的分量，四个人享用，的确是太多了，七姑奶奶有个计较，“都是自己人，不必客气。”她说：“留起一半吧！”就一半也还是多了些，胡雪岩吃了两小碗，摩腹说道：“我真饱了。”接着又问：“这何厨我以前怎么没有听说过？”“最近才从广州来。”古应春答说：“自己想开馆子，还没有谈拢。”“怎么叫还没有谈拢？”“有人出本钱，要谈条件。”“你倒问问他，肯不肯到我这里来。”胡雪岩说，“我现在就少个好厨子。”“好的。等我来问他。”
en: At this moment the shark's fin arrived, and Cook He came before the diners wearing a red-tasselled cap to pay his respects. Such was the custom when the principal dish was served; host and guests were expected to reward him. Hu, generous as ever, casually picked out a banknote for a hundred taels. “How can four people finish such a dish?” Luo asked. “I almost feel the expense on Seventh Sister's behalf.” The fin came on a silver platter two chi and five cun across, enough for twelve people. Four diners could hardly do justice to it. The Seventh Lady had a plan. “We are all friends. There is no need for ceremony. Let us put half aside.” Even half was rather too much. After two small bowls, Hu rubbed his stomach and declared himself full. He then asked why he had never heard of this cook before. “He has only recently arrived from Guangzhou,” Gu replied. “He wants to open a restaurant, but the arrangements have not yet been settled.” “What arrangements?” “Someone is offering the capital. They must agree on terms.” “Ask whether he would be willing to come to me. What I lack now is a good cook.” “Very well. I shall ask him.”

zh: 吃完饭围坐闲谈，钟打九点，七姑奶奶便催胡雪岩送罗四姐回家。在城开不夜的上海，这时还早得很，选歌征色、纸醉金迷的几处地方，如昼锦里等等“市面”还只刚刚开始。不过，胡雪岩与罗四姐心里都明白，这是七姑奶奶故意让他们有接近的机会，所以都未提出异议。临上轿时，七姑奶奶关照轿夫，将一具两展的大食盒，纳入轿箱，交代罗四姐说：“我们家人请人吃夜饭有规矩的，接下来要请吃消夜。今天我请你们小爷叔做主人，到你府上去请。食盒里一瓷坛的鱼翅，是先分出来的，不是吃剩的东西。”“谢谢，谢谢，”罗四姐说：“算你请胡大先生，我替你代做主人好了。”“随便你。”七姑奶奶笑道：“哪个是主，”哪个是客，你们自己去商量。“于是罗四姐开发了佣人的赏钱，与胡雪岩原轿归去。到家要忙着做主人，胡雪岩将她拦住了。“你不必忙，忙了半天，我根本吃不下，岂不是害你白忙，害我自己不安。依我说，你叫人泡壶好茶，我们谈谈天最好。”“那么，请到楼上去坐。”
en: After dinner they sat talking. When the clock struck nine, the Seventh Lady urged Hu to take Luo home. Nine was early in Shanghai, where the city remained awake through the night. In places such as Zhoujin Lane, devoted to song, women, and extravagant pleasure, business was only beginning. But both Hu and Luo understood that the Seventh Lady was deliberately giving them an opportunity to become closer, and neither objected. As they were entering their chairs, she told the bearers to place a large two-tier food box in the chair compartment. “In our household, inviting someone to dinner means inviting them to supper afterwards as well. Tonight I am asking Little Uncle to act as host at your house. There is a porcelain jar of shark's fin in the box. It was set aside beforehand; it is not leftovers.” “Thank you. Let us say that you are inviting Mr Hu, and I shall act as hostess for you.” The Seventh Lady laughed. “As you please. You can settle between yourselves who is host and who is guest.” Luo distributed tips to the servants, and she and Hu returned in the same chairs that had brought them. At home she began bustling about as hostess, but Hu stopped her. “There is no need. You would spend all that effort, and I could not eat another thing. It would only waste your time and make me uncomfortable. Have someone brew good tea, and let us talk.” “Then come upstairs.”

zh: 楼上明灯灿然，春风胎荡，四目相视，自然逗发了情思。罗四姐忽然觉得胸前有透不过气的感觉，忽忙挺起胸来，微仰着脸，连连吸气，才好过些。“你今年几岁？”她问。“四十出头了。”“看起来象四十不到。”罗四姐幽幽地叹了口气，“当初我那番心思，你晓得不晓得？”“怎么不晓得？”胡雪岩说：“我只当我们没有缘分，哪晓得现在会遇见，看起来缘分还在。”“可惜，我已经不是从前的我。‘人老珠黄不值钱’。”“ 这一点都不对，照我看，你比从前更加漂亮了，好比柿子，从前又青又硬，现在又红又软。”胡雪岩咽了口唾沫，“吃起来之甜，想都想得到的。”罗四姐瞟了他一眼，笑着骂了句：“馋相！”“罗四姐，”胡雪岩问道：“你记不记得，有年夏天，我替你送会饯去，只有你一个人在家……”
en: Upstairs the lamps shone brightly, and an atmosphere as warm as spring surrounded them. As their eyes met, affection naturally stirred. Luo suddenly felt a constriction in her chest. She straightened, lifted her face slightly, and drew several deep breaths before feeling better. “How old are you this year?” “A little over forty.” “You look younger than forty.” She sighed softly. “Did you know how I felt about you then?” “How could I not? I thought we were not destined for each other. Yet here we are again. It seems the bond remains.” “Unfortunately, I am no longer the woman I was. An ageing woman is like a yellowed pearl, no longer worth anything.” “Not true at all. To my eyes, you are more beautiful than before. Like a persimmon: once green and hard, now red and soft.” Hu swallowed. “One can imagine how sweet it would taste.” She glanced at him and laughingly called him greedy. “Sister Luo,” he asked, “do you remember a summer when I brought you the savings-club payment, and you were alone at home…?”
